title: 渡汉江
author: 宋之问
intro: After a long exile with no news from home, a man finally nears his village — and suddenly he is too afraid to ask anyone how his family is. A perfect picture of a feeling everyone knows.
analysis: 诗人被贬到岭南（五岭以南，今天的广东、广西一带），那时交通不便，和家里断了音信。他在那里过了一个冬天，又到了春天。后来他偷偷逃回北方，渡过汉江，离家越来越近了。按常理，离家越近应该越高兴、越着急打听消息，可是诗人说“近乡情更怯”——越靠近家乡，心里反而越害怕，连路上遇到从家乡来的人也不敢问。为什么？因为太久没有消息，他怕听到家人出事的坏消息。这种又盼又怕的矛盾心情，很多人都有过，诗人用十个字就说清楚了。“近乡情怯”今天已经成了成语，用来形容久别回乡时的复杂心情。
analysisEn:
The poet had been banished to Lingnan, the far south beyond the mountains (today’s Guangdong and Guangxi). Travel was slow and letters rarely arrived, so he lost all contact with his family. A winter passed there, and then a spring. At last he slipped away and headed north; crossing the Han River, he is getting close to home.

You would expect him to be excited and eager for news. Instead he says: “The nearer I get to home, the more timid I feel — I don’t dare ask the people coming from there.” Why? After so long without a word, any news could be bad news. As long as he doesn’t ask, everyone at home is still safe in his mind.

This mixture of hope and dread is something almost everyone has felt — waiting for exam results, opening a letter, coming back after years away. The poem catches it in ten characters, without a single difficult word. The phrase 近乡情怯 has become an idiom for the nervous, complicated feeling of returning home after a long absence.
background: Song Zhiwen (c. 656–712) was a leading court poet who helped shape the rules of Tang regulated verse. Exiled to the far south in 705 for his ties to Empress Wu’s favourites, he secretly fled back north the next year; the poem is traditionally dated to that journey. Some editions attribute it to the later poet Li Pin.
pronunciation: 无特殊读音。怯 qiè；复 fù。
version: 采用通行文本，全诗四句。重要异文：“岭外音书断”一作“岭外音书绝”。作者一说为李频（《全唐诗》两收），通行选本归宋之问。

lines.lit: Beyond the mountains, news and letters were cut off;
lines.en: Beyond the southern mountains, no letters reached me;

lines.lit: through winter and then through spring.
lines.en: a winter passed, and then a spring.

lines.lit: Nearing home, my feelings grow more timid;
lines.en: Now, close to home, I grow more afraid —

lines.lit: I don’t dare ask the people coming.
lines.en: I dare not ask the travellers coming from there.

words.en: beyond the mountain ranges — the far south
words.note: 五岭以南，古代是贬官去的偏远地方，也叫“岭南”。
现代汉语有“中断”“断了联系”。

words.en: growing timid as one nears home
words.note: 由这首诗来的成语，今天仍用。
现代汉语“来人”指派来的人，意思稍有不同。

imagery.name: 江
imagery.zh: 渡过汉江，意味着离家已经很近，情绪也到了最紧张的时候。
imagery.en: Crossing the Han River means home is near — the moment his nerves are tightest.

imagery.name: 春
imagery.zh: “经冬复历春”，季节轮换写出离家时间之久。
imagery.en: Winter turning into spring shows how long he has been cut off.
